name: Saint Peter Chrysologus
history: Bishop of Ravenna when it was the capital of the Western Empire, Peter was later called Chrysologus, golden word, for his preaching. Many of his sermons survive: short, vivid and full of love for the Incarnation and the Eucharist. He urged loyalty to the Bishop of Rome in matters of faith. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1729.
life: Peter was born at Imola and served its bishop as a deacon before being made bishop of Ravenna around 433. The imperial court was then at Ravenna, and the Empress Galla Placidia supported his building of churches and care for the city. His people loved his preaching, which was brief because, he said, he did not want to tire them. Around 180 of his sermons survive, on the Gospels, the Creed, the Lord’s Prayer and the mysteries of Christ’s birth, and he often turns to the Eucharist as the bread come down from heaven. When the monk Eutyches, condemned for teaching that Christ had only one nature, appealed to him, Peter replied that he should listen to the Bishop of Rome, through whom Saint Peter still teaches the faith to those who seek it. He died at Imola around 450. Benedict XIII named him a Doctor of the Church in 1729.
prayerTo: Saint Peter Chrysologus, golden-tongued preacher, you spoke briefly and lovingly of the mysteries of Christ. Pray for all who preach, that they may speak with clarity and warmth, and for me, that I may hunger for the Word and for the Bread of life. Amen.
penance: Pray the Our Father very slowly today, one phrase at a time, and give the price of a loaf of bread to a food bank.
meditation: He kept his sermons short for love of his hearers. How could you say what matters more simply today?
